Source: A 69-year-old man presents to clinic due to shortness of breath, worsening pain in his right shoulder, and episodes of hemoptysis.

Physical exam is notable for right pupillary constriction as well as paresthesias in his right fourth and fifth digits.
There is no pain with active shoulder rotation.
He routinely travels both domestically and internationally as a senior shipyard worker and has a 30-pack-year smoking history.

He has a history of coronary artery disease and underwent an uncomplicated coronary angioplasty with stent placement 2 years ago.
